text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.5% today to close at $133.76, extending a two-week decline of 9.6%. The immediate trigger is a sharp drop in global oil prices: Brent crude dipped below $90 a barrel on Monday for the first time since August, driven by comments from President Trump suggesting the Iran conflict could end soon and Tehran's military capacity is degraded. Since oil refiners and producers earn more when crude prices are higher, the prospect of de-escalation and lower energy prices weighs directly on the company's profitability outlook.

The stock has been sliding since early November, when the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The combination of weaker crude prices and whatever signals came from those results has pushed the stock down steadily over the past week, even as US oil (at $99.64 a barrel today) holds somewhat firmer than global Brent crude.
